channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Cash incentive for CRSB Certified beef producers launched
item.description: The Canadian Roundtable for Sustainable Beef (CRSB) has launched an incentive payment for CRSB Certified producers.

item.title: Top potash producer Nutrien misses fourth-quarter profit estimates
item.description: Nutrien missed analysts’ expectations for fourth-quarter profit on Wednesday, as lower sales in its crop nutrients business weighed on the world’s top potash producer.

item.title: Bayer: glyphosate shortages not expected outside U.S. after Trump invokes Defense Production Act to secure supply
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday signed an executive order invoking the Defense Production Act to ensure an adequate U.S. supply of elemental phosphorus and glyphosate-based herbicides, the White House said.

item.title: International trade minister visits Singapore, Vietnam
item.description: Canada’s minister of international trade met with Vietnam and Singapore government officials to emphasize the need for free trade, highlight Canadian agri-food products, and to announce projects aimed at strenghtening trade with those nations.

item.title: Minor tweaks in AAFC supply and demand report
item.description: There were only small changes in the latest supply and demand estimates from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada released on Feb. 18.

item.title: Urea market expected to remain tight in 2026
item.description: Nitrogen fertilizer markets will remain tight in 2026 but one analyst thinks urea prices will peak in Feb/Mar and then subside a bit.

item.title: How China plans to dominate global trade long after Trump
item.description: Beijing is exploiting Trump-era uncertainty to stitch its manufacturing base into the world’s biggest economic blocs, aiming to end decades of U.S. trade leverage.

item.title: Wheat breeder loses faith in Canada’s system
item.description: Richard Cuthbert, a former AAFC wheat breeder in Swift Current, resigned from his job in January because he believed he could “no longer be productive.”

item.title: Canada needs an agriculture strategy to rebuild trust with producers, investors and trade partners: report
item.description: Canada needs a national agriculture strategy with clear priorities and results according to a new report from the Canada West Foundation.

item.title: Increased demand only way out of supply glut
item.description: Grain markets are still suffering from a supply glut. The only way out of it is to increase demand, says the USDA’s chief economist.
